title: Indian-Origin Doctor Leads US Team in Creating New Framework to Treat Liver Cancer
excerpt: Dr. Amit G. Singal of UT Southwestern spearheaded BEACON-HCC, a treatment allocation system backed by 17 cancer centers that replaces the 30-year-old Barcelona Clinic guidelines.
body:
• Indian-origin hepatologist Dr. Amit G. Singal led a consortium of 20 experts from 17 cancer centers to create BEACON-HCC, a new treatment framework for liver cancer
  • The framework, published in Hepatology, achieved 96.6% agreement with expert treatment decisions versus just 72.4% for the existing Barcelona Clinic system
  • BEACON-HCC incorporates newer therapies including radiation and immunotherapy combinations that the 30-year-old BCLC system does not fully address

A New Standard for Liver Cancer Treatment

Indian-origin hepatologist Dr. Amit G. Singal, medical director of the Liver Tumor Program and chief of hepatology at UT Southwestern Medical Center in Dallas, has led a team of 20 experts from 17 major cancer centers across North America and Europe in developing a new treatment framework for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the most common form of primary liver cancer.

The resource, called BEACON-HCC (Best Evidence and North American Consensus on Treatment Allocation for Hepatocellular Carcinoma), was published on August 7 in the journal Hepatology by HCC-LIVE, a consortium of North American HCC specialists. It represents the most significant overhaul of liver cancer treatment guidance in nearly three decades.

Why the Old System Fell Short

For almost 30 years, clinicians worldwide have relied on the Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) staging and treatment allocation system to guide HCC management. But as new therapies have emerged—including external beam radiation, transarterial radioembolization, and immune-based drug combinations—a growing gap has opened between what the old guidelines recommend and what specialized cancer centers actually practice.

\"The BCLC does not elevate all of the treatment paradigms that we have available to us, and promotes treatment decisions that are somewhat different from how we have practiced at our institution.\"

— Dr. Mark Yarchoan, Associate Professor of Oncology, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine

The idea for BEACON-HCC emerged as Dr. Yarchoan, co-author Dr. Jeffrey Meyer, and their colleagues at Johns Hopkins recognized their management of HCC patients was increasingly diverging from BCLC recommendations. For example, BCLC classifies tumors that invade blood vessels as advanced disease and recommends systemic therapy alone—but in modern practice, vascular invasion does not necessarily mean remission is out of reach.

How BEACON-HCC Works

BEACON-HCC incorporates tumor burden, vascular invasion, tumor biology, liver function, and overall patient health into a comprehensive framework. It recognizes emerging modalities that the older system sidelined: external beam radiation therapy, transarterial radioembolization (which delivers radioactive beads directly into blood vessels feeding a tumor), and novel combination immunotherapy regimens.

The framework was validated using 29 de-identified patient cases reviewed independently by both the 20 co-authors and 18 external HCC experts not involved in its development. Treatment decisions aligned with BEACON-HCC recommendations 96.6% of the time, compared to just 72.4% agreement with BCLC 2025 recommendations.

The Scale of the Problem

HCC is the third-leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide and the leading cause of cancer death in patients with cirrhosis. Despite improvements in screening and treatment, the five-year survival rate for HCC remains below 25%, according to Johns Hopkins. Contributing cancer centers to the BEACON-HCC framework include UT Southwestern, Johns Hopkins, UCLA, Mayo Clinic, NYU Langone Health, University of Michigan, University of Chicago, Northwestern University, and Hospital Universitario Vall d'Hebron in Barcelona, Spain.

Indian-American Leadership in Oncology

Dr. Singal's role as lead author on the BEACON-HCC framework underscores the growing influence of Indian-American physicians in shaping cancer treatment standards in the United States. As a Dedman Family Scholar in Clinical Care and holder of the Willis C. Maddrey Distinguished Chair in Liver Disease at UT Southwestern, Singal has built a career focused on HCC screening, risk stratification, and treatment optimization.

\"As systemic and locoregional therapies continue to evolve, BEACON-HCC provides a dynamic, adaptable framework that can grow alongside our expanding therapeutic armamentarium for HCC.\"

— Dr. Marina Baretti, Assistant Professor of Oncology, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine

The BEACON-HCC team hopes the framework will influence how clinicians worldwide think about liver cancer management, providing a practical tool for tumor boards and multidisciplinary clinic discussions as treatment options continue to expand.
